## Duplication (Q4)

- 31,446 groups of byte-identical objects
- 5,041 of those span more than one bucket
- 47,736 objects are redundant copies

Detail in `data/manifests/duplicate-candidates.json`. Note these are ETag matches,
which catch byte-identical files only. The same document scanned twice, or saved
under different PDF producers, will not match here — that is what content-hash
dedup on extracted text is for (CLAUDE.md §5).

## Prefix structure (Q3)

> **Redacted for the public version of this repo.** The original section listed the top
> twelve prefixes per bucket, two levels deep. Real folder names revealed private material
> (correspondence, organizational finances, personal names), so they are summarized here
> by pattern instead. The generator in `scripts/s3_corpus_summary.py` is unchanged.

What the prefix trees showed, bucket by bucket:

- **Whole-server FTP backups dominate the website buckets.** Four buckets hold dated backup
  trees (`<year>FTParchive/`, `ftpArchive<year>/`, `<year>BackUp/`) that contain the CMS
  itself, its admin endpoints, and server statistics alongside the published content. This
  is the finding behind decision 0008: the buckets are server backups, not content exports.
- **Prefixes encode the source site only at the bucket level.** Inside a bucket, folders are
  organized by topic or by whoever uploaded them, not by URL path. Original URLs can be
  reconstructed for the web-root trees but not for the loose resource folders.
- **There is no date structure and no manifest file.** Dates must come from document
  metadata or `LastModified`, which reflects upload time, not publication.
- **`www.forest-library.example` is a personal research archive, not a website.** Its top
  prefixes are topical collections — history, photos, FOIA responses, agency reports,
  academic papers — plus an email archive (~39,000 objects) and a folder explicitly marked
  not-public. Those last two are why decision 0008 excludes `.eml` pending consent.
- **`www.timberland-network.example` is a raw WordPress install** plus a zipped hosting-provider
  site export, which together account for ~75% of its objects.
- **`www.clearcut-watch.example` is flat and small**, organized by mill or tract name.
- **`Publications` holds seven presentation files** under a single prefix.

## Open questions carried forward

- Is www.timberland-network.example the seventh site, and do we want the WordPress dump or a fresh extraction?
- What are the ~29,000 .eml files in www.forest-library.example, and is any of that correspondence publishable? Default: excluded until the founder says otherwise.
- What is the 'Publications' bucket and who created it?
- No bucket exists for field-notes.example or canopy-archive.example — both need fresh scrapes.
